COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPCRL No. 838 of 2026 
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Rajveer Singh, learned counsel for 
the petitioners and Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned 
A.G.A. for the State. 
2. After post lunch session, Mr. Tumul 
Nainwal, learned A.G.A. for the State apprised 
to this Court that the birth certificate of the 
petitioner no.1 was sent for verification today 
itself to the concerned SHO and on verification, 
he has apprised that the documents furnished 
before the authority, the school leaving 
certificate wherein the date of birth of the 
petitioner no.1 is shown as 20.07.2007. He 
also apprised that concerned official also visited 
Govt. Girls Junior High School from where, it 
has been apprised that as per the original 
record, the date of birth of the petitioner no.1 is 
20.07.2010. 
3. Admittedly, there are some discrepancies 
in the date of birth of the petitioner no.1. Her 
parents, who are present in Court submits that 
they married in the year 2009, therefore, there 
is no question that the petitioner no.1 was born 
in 2007. If it is so, it certainly creates doubt 
about the age of petitioner no.1, therefore, to 
examine her correct age, she has to go with 
some medical tests. 
4. In such view of the matter, the petitioner 
no.1 is directed to be sent to Nari Niketan of the 
concerned district. The Police officials are 
directed to take her in protection and sent her  to Nari Niketan. The Superintendent of Nari 
Niketan is also directed to immediately contact 
with the concerned Chief Medical Officer to 
make an arrangement for medical examination 
of the petitioner no.1 and submit his report 
within a week. 
5. The parents of the petitioner no.1 are also 
agree for medical examination and till then, she 
may be sent to the Nari Niketan. 
6. So far as the petitioner no.2 is concerned, 
Mr. Rajveer Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioner undertakes that on the next date, the 
petitioner no.2 will remain present in Court. 
7. The In-charge Circle Officer, High Court is 
directed to send the petitioner no.1 with the 
assistance of some lady police officer under 
protection 
8. Put up on 08.07.2026. 
9. Copy of this order be supplied to Mr. 
Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. for the State so 
that he may send it to the concerned official for 
necessary compliance. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
 26.05.2026 Shiv/

Vaishali
--Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Rajveer Singh, learned counsel 
for the petitioners through Video 
Conferencing.
2. Mr. Rakesh Joshi, learned A.G.A. 
along with Mr. Manoj Bhatt, learned Brief 
Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Bilal Ahmed, learned counsel for 
respondent no.4.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners 
would submit that, vide order dated 
26.05.2026, this Court, noticing the 
dispute regarding the date of birth of 
petitioner no.1 and, as per the records of 
the School Leaving Certificate, finding her 
to be below 16 years of age, directed that 
petitioner no.1 be sent to Nari Niketan. It 
is submitted that, since then, petitioner 
no.1 has been residing at the concerned 
Nari Niketan.
5. Today, respondent no.4, who is the 
father of petitioner no.1, and the mother 
of petitioner no.1 are present in person 
before the Court. They submit that their  daughter, i.e. petitioner no.1, has called 
them from Nari Niketan and expressed 
her willingness to return home.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the 
petitioners would submit that petitioner 
no.1 has categorically refused even to talk 
to her parents.
7. Be that as it may, since petitioner 
no.1 is presently residing at Nari Niketan 
in compliance with the order dated 
26.05.2026, the Superintendent of the 
concerned Nari Niketan is directed to 
produce petitioner no.1 before this Court 
on the next date of listing, i.e. 
22.09.2026.
8. List this case on 22.09.2026.
9. The parents of petitioner no.1 shall 
also remain present before the Court on 
the date fixed.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 16-09-2026

WPCRL/838/2026
Vaishali
--Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Rajveer Singh, Advocate for the petitioner. 
Mr. S.C. Dumka, A.G.A. for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
Mr. Bilal Ahmed, Advocate for respondent no.3.
2. In sequel to the order dated 16.09.2026, 
petitioner no.1 and her parents are present before the 
Court today. Petitioner no.1 has been brought before 
the Court in the custody of L.C. No.184, Nikita, from 
Nari Niketan, Dehradun.
3. This Court interacted with petitioner no.1 and 
her parents in the Chamber. During the interaction, 
petitioner no.1 expressed her willingness to go with 
her parents. Her parents have also given an 
undertaking before this Court that they are willing to 
take petitioner no.1 with them and shall ensure that 
she is not harassed, ill-treated or victimized in any 
manner. Petitioner no.1 has, in turn, undertaken that 
she shall respect her parents and shall not indulge in 
any act or conduct which may cause annoyance or 
inconvenience to them.
4. Since there is a dispute regarding the age of 
petitioner no.1, inasmuch as, different dates of birth 
are reflected in her school leaving certificate, birth 
certificate, Parivar Register and Aadhaar Card, and a 
Coordinate Bench of this Court has earlier directed 
determination of her age, this Court considers it 
appropriate that an ossification test of petitioner no.1 
be conducted for the purpose of assisting in 
determination of her age. 5. Accordingly, the parents of petitioner no.1 are 
directed to take petitioner no.1 to the office of the 
Chief Medical Officer, Haridwar, for undergoing the 
ossification test on 30.09.2026. The Station House 
Officer, Police Station Laksar, District Haridwar, shall 
depute a responsible police officer to accompany 
petitioner no.1 and her parents and ensure their safe 
transit and appearance before the concerned medical 
authority for conducting the aforesaid test.
6. The Chief Medical Officer, Haridwar, shall 
ensure that the ossification test is conducted on the 
date fixed and the report thereof is forwarded to this 
Court through the office of the Government Advocate, 
Uttarakhand, before the next date of listing.
7. In view of the statement and undertaking given 
by petitioner no.1 and her parents before the Court, 
the custody of petitioner no.1 is handed over to her 
parents, subject to their undertaking that petitioner 
no.1 shall not be harassed, ill-treated or victimized by 
them. The parents shall also ensure her safety, well￾being and proper care.
8. Learned State Counsel is directed to 
communicate this order forthwith to the Chief Medical 
Officer, Haridwar, as well as the Station House 
Officer, Police Station Laksar, District Haridwar, for 
necessary compliance.
9. List this matter on 13.10.2026.
 
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 
 22.09.2026
Arpan
